'''''Rumex palustris''''', or '''marsh dock''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17 }}</ref> is a plant species of the genus ''[[Rumex]]'', found in [[Europe]]. The species is a dicot belonging to the family [[Polygonaceae]]. The species [[epithet]] ''palustris'' is Latin for "of the marsh" which indicates its common habitat.<ref>Archibald William Smith {{google books|ahNMkgoNJ7IC|A Gardener's Handbook of Plant Names: Their Meanings and Origins|page=258}}</ref>

==Description==

''Rumex palustris'' is an herb that can be perennial, biennial, or annual.<ref>{{PLANTS|id=RUPA12|taxon=Rumex palustris|accessdate=26 October 2015}}</ref> The stem is upwardly inclined and bears sparse hairy protuberances.<ref>Dawson, J.E. 1979. A biosystematic study of Rumex section Rumex in Canada and the United States.Ph.D. thesis. Carleton University, Ottawa.</ref> The stem is less than one meter tall. The branch attachment is alternate. The basal leaves are lanceolate; they are broader in the middle and taper to a pointed end.  The cauline leaves are also lanceolate. The inflorescence consists of whorls with reddish-brown flowers. The root is wider at the middle and tapers towards the end.

This species' diploid number is 60.<ref>{{Cite journal|author=Strid, A.|author2=Andersson, I.A.|date=1985|title=Chromosome numbers of Greek mountain plants. An annotated list of 115 species.|journal=Botanische Jahrbücher für Systematik, Pflanzengeschichte und Pflanzengeographie|volume=1-127, 1881-2009|via=Tropicos}}</ref>

==Taxonomy==
The species name was first mentioned by [[Leonard Plukenet]], based on a collection made by [[Isaac Rand]].<ref name=":0">{{cite DNB|wstitle=Rand, Isaac|last=Boulger|first=George Simonds|authorlink=George Simonds Boulger|volume=47}}</ref> The authority of the accepted description, ''Rumex palustris'', was [[James Edward Smith (botanist)|James Edward Smith]], in Fl. Brit. volume 1, on page 394 in 1800.<ref name=":1">{{cite web|url=http://www.theplantlist.org/tpl1.1/record/kew-2424686|title=Rumex palustris Sm. is an accepted name|date=23 March 2012|publisher=theplantlist.org|access-date=10 October 2017}}</ref><ref name="ipni">{{cite web|url=http://www.ipni.org/ipni/idPlantNameSearch.do?id=697375-1|title=Polygonaceae Rumex palustris Sm.|publisher=ipni.org|access-date=10 October 2017}}</ref>

==Habitat and distribution==
''Rumex palustris'' can be found in wetlands such as moist meadows, marshes, lake shores and the shallow edges of streams. It is native to Europe and is concentrated in the Southeastern and Middle parts of the continent.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.gbif.org/species/4037603|title=Rumex palustris Sm.|website=www.gbif.org|access-date=2019-10-06}}</ref> The species was also introduced to America; it now grows in California and New Jersey.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://plants.usda.gov/plant-profile?symbol=RUPA12|title=Plants Profile for Rumex palustris (marsh dock)|website=plants.usda.gov|access-date=2019-10-06}}</ref>
